RoR is a nice little rougelike game that hits most of the right notes when it comes to making a good game.

Pros
+ various classes with different and unique playstyles
+ interesting equipment and items
+ level design is okay
+ enemies are very unique but could do better
+ excellent music and sound design 
+ story/lore is pretty good even though it is very minimal
+ controls are decent but sometimes it is a problem when doing platforming sections

Cons
- LAN and internet play are horrible and needs extra tinkering jsut to play with friends. Badly needs a lobby system and not the current one which requires IP address
- graphics and aesthetics could be better instead of pixel art
- optimization is okay I guess but it runs into problems once you start racking in various items and monsters flooding the screen

This is difficult because there is a lot of love for this game. I enjoyed most of my time with it, but ultimately, cannot recommend it. The camera feels very zoomed out (even when I zoom in), making some of the wonderfully-made pixel art difficult to really appreciate. There are alot of items, but few are really memorable. I always was looking for item-triggered excitement similiar to how I would feel in BOI when getting a super powerful weapon. Not the case here. The alternate playable characters have very different playstyle that is probably cool, but once I beat the game I had little interest in really fleshing that out.

My number one complaint is that the entire game feels *really* grindy: its just unleashing a bullet-hell on monsters, retreat to refill the meters, and repeat.

I never tried multiplayer.

[i]Risk of Rain[/i] is a sci-fi platforming roguelike where you pick a character and run through levels while collecting a massive selection of (stackable) items to make yourself stronger and more likely to survive long enough to find a way home. The catch is that the more time you spend alive, the more numerous and difficult the enemies become, so there is a trade-off between mining levels for items and speedrunning. Any fan of [i]Spelunky[/i] will appreciate its extraplanetary equivalent, but there are a few less-than-desirable traits which should be of note.

Unlike [i]Spelunky, Risk of Rain[/i] has a diverse set of classes from whom to choose. However, I believe they could be placed on a bit more equal footing. Where many games of all kinds, from [i]TF2[/i] to [i]The Binding of Isaac,[/i] make sure that different classes are well balanced, [i]Risk of Rain[/i] has certain characters which are clearly far worse than the others (no matter what one's individual strategy may be). Contrary to the achievement name, you [i]will[/i] find the Robot Janitor, and you [i]will[/i] regret it. Classes like the Enforcer or the Robot Janitor are simply too slow to stand any chance against mid-game swarms of enemies. They are, indeed, powerful classes, but the level difficulty ramps up too quickly to avoid the swarms (whether you choose to search for items or speedjogataleisurelypace). If you do not quickly find several of the same very specific items, you will die more frustrated than entertained. The other "weaker" classes have some method of teleporting or defense-rolling to safety, but there is no health pool large enough to save you from enemies too numerous to kill and too fast for you to run away. That said, playing as the other classes yields a roguelike challenge with items and enemies worth the time and money.

Overall, [i]Risk of Rain[/i] is a good game with uniquely designed aesthetics and gameplay mechanics. This sci-fi roguelike poses a challenge which, though sometimes frustrating, still maintains considerable replay value.
8.5/10
